title: Geo fairness proxy with adaptive pacing and SLO broker
creator: Maya Fernández
description: Design and implement a lightweight proxy component (Geo Fairness Proxy) that brokers per-tenant SLOs into region selection decisions. The proxy enforces fairness across regions by combining latency headroom, remaining capacity credits, and tenant-specified locality preferences. It also implements adaptive pacing (per-tenant, per-region token buckets), an in-flight hedging shepherd, and circuit-breaker hooks for graceful load shedding.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic route (10% of requests for a single tenant) evaluated for 48h without increase in 99th tail latency beyond 5% versus baseline
Per-tenant SLO mapping endpoint returns region scores and chosen region IDs within 3ms median processing time
Automatic shedding triggers when regional capacity_credit drops below threshold and shed rate monitored in metrics dashboard
Hedged request cancellation reduces wasted duplicate tokens by >= 70% after primary completes
End-to-end integration tests exercising circuit-breaker open/close and fallback to secondary region pass in CI
Documentation page (Confluence) with API, operator knobs, and runbook exists and is linked from Console rollout page
technical_notes: SLO broker: translate tenant SLOs (latency target, error budget window) into numeric headroom and priority weight. Headroom = target - observed_p95 * safety_factor
Region score = alpha*(latency_headroom_normalized) + beta*(capacity_credit_normalized) + gamma*(geo_preference_score). Tunable weights via experiment flag.
Adaptive pacing: token-bucket per (tenant, region) seeded from capacity_credit. Refill rate decays proportionally with observed queueing delay to favor low-latency paths.
Circuit breakers: two-layer thresholds. Local gate tracks region-specific overloads (qps, cpu, queue_length). Global gate enforces tenant-level safety (aggregate error budget).

In-flight hedging shepherd: if a hedged request is dispatched, cancel hedges when primary returns within cancel_window; if not, allow hedge to proceed. Cancellation uses best-effort gRPC cancel + opaque task-id to serving runtime.
Observability hooks: emit region_score breakdown, decision_trace (reason codes), token_bucket_state, and circuit_breaker_state on each request sample to tracing/metrics.
Failover logic: prefer soft-fallback (route to next best region) with exponential backoff on retries; hard-fallback only when multiple consecutive circuit opens detected.
Performance budget: broker must not add >5ms median latency to request path when colocated with request director; otherwise run as async cache with fast-path TTLs.
Security: tenant preferences validated against RBAC; proxy runs in dedicated namespace for Dedicated deployments and honors VPC/private network constraints.
implementation_plan: Prototype SLO broker algorithm in python (not in-path) and run simulation against historical traffic traces (1 week) to tune alpha/beta/gamma
Introduce region_score grpc API and a lightweight C++ proxy shim for low-latency path (for hosted and dedicated).
Implement adaptive pacing token-buckets and persistence of capacity_credit in Redis with TTL and optimistic update strategy.
Add circuit-breaker primitives to request director: local and global gates + counters exposed to runtime telemetry.
Integrate hedging shepherd: unique request-id propagation, cancellation path, metric emission for duplicate suppression.
Add CI e2e tests: overload a synthetic region, assert shedding and fallback behavior, assert no SLO regressions beyond allowed limits.
Create Confluence design doc, console feature flag, and admin knobs for ops to tune in production.
Coordinate with infra team to provide extra sampling dashboards and alerting (pager thresholds) during canary.
Ship initial canary behind feature flag and monitor for 72h; iterate on weights and shedding thresholds.
Post-canary cleanup and add to release notes and runbooks.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal staging with synthetic traffic (QA) — validate correctness and no regressions
Stage 1: Canary to 3 production tenants (10% of their traffic) in us-west-2 for 48 hours
Stage 2: Expand to 10 tenants across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 while monitoring SLO breach rates
Stage 3: Gradually open to all tenants in a single region with operator-observed stability for 7 days
Stage 4: Global switch with per-tenant opt-in and automatic rollback if tenant SLO breach increases >1.5x baseline
Operator knobs exposed: alpha/beta/gamma weights, capacity_credit_window, shed_threshold_pct, hedge_cancel_window_ms
metrics: tenant.slo.compliance.rate (daily) — fraction of tenants within SLO
region.score.breakdown (histogram of latency_headroom vs capacity_credit contributions)
hedge.duplicate_waste_ratio — tokens wasted by hedges / total tokens
observability.signal: tracing sample contains decision_trace id for at least 1% traffic to debug edge cases
risks: Decision path adds latency to hot requests: mitigate by micro-optimizing C++ path or falling back to an async cached verdict
Tuning complexity: alpha/beta/gamma might interact badly with auto-scaling leading to oscillations. Mitigate with hysteresis and decay windows.
Cross-tenant fairness tradeoff: high-priority tenants could starve others if capacity credits not normalized. Use per-region fairness caps and global reservoir.
Observability blind spots: insufficient sampling will make root cause analysis slow. Mitigate by higher sampling rates during canary.
Edge case: network partition between proxy and region metrics store could cause incorrect capacity_credit reads; fallback to conservative safe mode (reduce weights on capacity).
